name: Marital Games
oneLine: Corner, Courtroom, Frigid Woman/Man, Harried, If It Weren't For You, Look How Hard I've Tried, and Sweetheart are games built for the long-running intimacy of a marriage or household.
whatYouDid: You found the antithesis to Sweetheart's public needle ("Yes, honey!") and to Courtroom's third-person appeal (handing the case back to the two people actually in it), and caught Alisha's If It Weren't For You at the exact moment her stated obstacle disappeared.

fromBook.quote: the one-time Rescuer changes to an accusing Persecutor instead of a woeful Victim

expand.definition: Marital games recur because the relationship gives them an unlimited run of replays: Sweetheart folds a public jab inside praise, Courtroom recruits a third party as judge instead of talking directly, If It Weren't For You racketeers about an obstacle that turns out not to be the real one, and Look How Hard I've Tried - which TA Today calls See How Hard I've Tried - starts in Rescuer and switches to an accusing Persecutor instead of a Victim.
expand.otherFraming: TA Today prefers to group these by Drama Triangle switch pattern rather than by name alone - Look How Hard I've Tried and I'm Only Trying To Help You share an opening Rescuer position and differ only in which role the player switches into.
expand.tryThisToday: Notice the next time a household complaint has the same shape it had last month, word for word - that repetition is the signature of a Marital game, not a new argument.
